bottlenecks: DecisionEngine.recommend() is purely rule-based with hardcoded thresholds (soil_moisture<0.2, temperature>38, etc.) — the `algorithm` constructor parameter is accepted but never used to select an ML path, so all recommendations are static if/else rules regardless of configuration
Confidence score is computed as min(1.0, len(recommendations)*0.2+0.3) — a heuristic based on rule count, not a calibrated model probability, making it unreliable for ranking or thresholding
Feature importance is hardcoded to mirror rule-trigger weights (0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1) rather than learned from data, so it does not reflect true feature contributions
API gateway has no rate limiting middleware — security.py implements check_rate_limit() but it is never wired into create_app(), leaving the API open to abuse
API gateway authentication defaults to open: when auth=None, _authenticate returns {sub:anonymous, roles:[admin]} — a fail-closed design would reject or use a minimal role
TenantRegistry uses in-memory dicts/lists for all state (tenants, farms, readings, commands) — no persistence, no horizontal scalability, data lost on restart
AuditLogger stores all events in an in-memory list with no eviction — unbounded memory growth in long-running processes; archive_old_events exists but is never called automatically
list_readings and list_commands in api_gateway filter only by farm_id, not tenant_id — a cross-tenant farm_id guess could leak data; the tenant check is only on the path param, not the data scope
No async support in DecisionEngine — recommend() is synchronous and blocks the event loop when called from async FastAPI endpoints
Dashboard broadcast() iterates all WebSocket clients sequentially with no backpressure — a slow client can delay updates for all others
Rate limiting state in security.py (_rate_limits dict) is per-process in-memory — not shared across multiple API instances or workers
No caching layer for recommendations — identical FarmState inputs recompute from scratch every time
missing_algorithms: No ML-based recommendation path — ml_models.py provides LinearRegressionModel, DecisionTreeClassifier, IsolationForestModel, and YieldPredictor, but DecisionEngine never imports or uses them; the two subsystems are disconnected
No A/B testing framework — no experiment assignment, no traffic splitting, no statistical significance testing for comparing recommendation strategies
No feature store — FeatureEngine computes GDD, VPD, and trend features but there is no persistence, versioning, or retrieval layer for serving features to models at inference time
No model versioning in the serving path — ModelRegistry tracks versions but DecisionEngine and the API gateway always use a hardcoded default model with no version selection or rollback
No drift detection — no monitoring of input feature distributions or prediction distributions over time, no statistical tests (KS, PSI) for data or concept drift
No ensemble or hybrid approach — recommendations cannot combine rule-based and ML outputs (e.g., rules for safety-critical thresholds, ML for yield optimization)
No time-series forecasting — no ARIMA, Prophet, or LSTM-based forecasting for predicting future soil moisture, temperature, or pest pressure
No optimization algorithms — no linear programming or constraint solver for irrigation scheduling, fertilizer planning, or resource allocation under constraints
No anomaly detection in the recommendation pipeline — IsolationForestModel exists but is never used to flag anomalous sensor readings before they trigger recommendations
No reinforcement learning or multi-armed bandit — no exploration/exploitation mechanism to learn which recommendations improve outcomes over time
No causal inference — no uplift modeling or counterfactual analysis to estimate the true effect of a recommendation (e.g., did irrigation actually improve yield?)
No feedback loop — RecommendationResult has no outcome tracking, so the system cannot measure whether recommendations were followed or whether they worked
No model performance monitoring — no logging of prediction accuracy, no alerting when model degrades, no automated retraining triggers
No canary or shadow deployment — no mechanism to serve a new model version to a subset of traffic for validation before full rollout
benchmark_gaps: No offline evaluation metrics for recommendations — no precision, recall, NDCG, or mean reciprocal rank computed against historical outcomes
No online metrics tracking — no measurement of recommendation click-through rate, action completion rate, or user satisfaction
No model performance baselines — no stored baseline accuracy for yield prediction or anomaly detection to compare new models against
No load or stress testing for the API gateway — no benchmarks for requests/sec, latency percentiles, or breaking points under concurrent load
No regression tests for model accuracy — tests verify model training/prediction mechanics but do not assert minimum accuracy thresholds on fixed datasets
No fairness or bias testing — no checks for disparate recommendation quality across crop types, farm sizes, or geographic regions
No latency SLO tests — no assertions that recommend() or API endpoints complete within a target latency budget
No throughput benchmarks for the audit logger — no measurement of events/sec capacity or chain verification cost at scale
No chaos or failure-mode tests — no tests for behavior when ML model is untrained, when feature store is unavailable, or when audit logger fails
No integration tests exercising the full path from sensor reading → alert → recommendation → notification — each subsystem is tested in isolation
